allow_large: Owner asked for this change (2026-10-08): a new forge.toml runner setting and a forge init option, written into the generated workflow and reported by doctor and close
done_when: forge.toml has a runner setting (default ubuntu-latest, so nothing changes for repos that don't set it) that forge sync writes into every runs-on line of the generated forge.yml; forge init takes it as an option; the generated jobs' steps work on a plain self-hosted Linux runner (uv and Node installed by their setup actions, nothing assumed from GitHub's hosted image); forge doctor and close's check wait say plainly when a pull request's checks have stayed queued with no runner picking them up for several minutes, naming the runner setting; the coordinator guide documents the setting; command tests cover a new repo initialised with a self-hosted runner and an existing repo adopted on an earlier release that sets it and syncs, plus the queued-without-a-runner message with a faked GitHub

findings.body: The wait still blocks on every reported check, but this guard considers only names listed in forge.toml. When `tests` and `forge-pr-check` are green while an additional `lint` check has been queued for over five minutes, `queued_reason` is never called. Close waits until its timeout and reports only that lint is queued, omitting the runner guidance. The changed `_pending_check_not_named` case already establishes that additional queued checks block close. Include those queued states when deciding whether to request the diagnostic.
findings.title: Diagnose queued checks outside the configured check names

why: The CI workflow Forge generates hard-codes runs-on: ubuntu-latest for both jobs, so in an organisation whose repos can only use self-hosted runners every new client repo's tests and forge-pr-check jobs stay queued forever, forge close waits on them indefinitely and no item can become ready; checks = [] is no way out because close refuses with no checks (owner report, 2026-10-08)
